notes:
Benchmark (a) uses this part as its astable timer at a 9 V supply.

RthetaJA is Section 5.4's P (PDIP) column, 98.5 degC/W, read from the rendered page. That table spans six packages across four devices under merged header cells, which the PDF text layer flattens; on the page, the P (PDIP) column is the only PDIP column and sits alone under the NA555, NE555 header.

The comparator levels (THRES, TRIG), the CONT open-circuit voltage, and VOH and VOL carry both datasheet columns, VCC = 5 V and VCC = 15 V, as condition arrays (AMB-127 item 2). Benchmark (a) runs at 9 V, between the two, and neither column describes it: a check needs both to bound the 9 V behaviour instead of silently picking one. The divider spread a timing model draws from these levels, and whether the two comparators' errors are correlated, are modelling choices the vendor does not state, so they are not recorded here (tests/benchmarks/derive-555-windows.py states its own). THRES current, TRIG current and the RESET voltage level have no VCC row: Section 5.5 (page 5) states each once, under its header's conditions (VCC = 5 V to 15 V, TA = 25 degC), so each is one Measure with no vcc condition rather than a 5 V figure. Supply current is stated per output state at both columns, four modes (page 6).

OUT is recorded as role 'output' (push-pull) while DISCH is 'open_collector'. Both come from the same device, and the distinction is precisely what the T2 lattice needs to check the two pins differently.

provenance.note: Record default. This datasheet covers four devices (NA555, NE555, SA555, SE555); every value recorded here is the NE555 column, and device-specific limits are noted where the columns differ.

/modes.locator: Section 5.5 Electrical Characteristics, Supply current rows (output low, no load)
/modes.note: IMPORTANT for benchmark (a), which runs this part at 9 V: the datasheet characterises supply current only at 5 V and 15 V. There is no 9 V row, and none of the recorded modes describes the benchmark's operating point. A current budget at 9 V must bound the draw between these two points or declare an interpolation; it must not silently pick one. Recording only the measured points, rather than an interpolated 9 V figure, is what forces that choice to be explicit.

/modes/0.locator: Section 5.5 Electrical Characteristics (continued), page 6, Supply current, Output high, no load, VCC = 15V row, NA555, NE555, SA555 column
/modes/0.note: The output-high rows, transcribed from the 2026-10-24 retrieval of the same SLFS022K revision. Supply current is published per output state, and supply-current-per-mode is an R29a field family on a record a benchmark picks, so both states are recorded at both columns. The output-low modes are the original transcription under /modes.

/modes/1.locator: Section 5.5 Electrical Characteristics (continued), page 6, Supply current, Output high, no load, VCC = 5V row, NA555, NE555, SA555 column
/modes/1.note: The output-high rows, transcribed from the 2026-10-24 retrieval of the same SLFS022K revision. Supply current is published per output state, and supply-current-per-mode is an R29a field family on a record a benchmark picks, so both states are recorded at both columns. The output-low modes are the original transcription under /modes.

/pins.locator: Table 4-1 Pin Functions; Section 5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings; Section 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions; Section 5.5 Electrical Characteristics
/pins.note: DISCH is recorded with role open_collector because Table 4-1 describes it verbatim as an 'Open collector output'. That role is load-bearing: it tells the ERC lattice this pin drives low only and requires an external pull-up, which is exactly how benchmark (a) uses it. The locator names every section the values under /pins are read from. It previously named only the pin-function table and one electrical section, while abs-max and recommended-operating values under the same pointer come from other tables the record itself cites for sibling values -- so a reviewer following it landed in a table that does not contain the number.

/pins/0/characteristics/open_circuit_vol.locator: Section 5.5 Electrical Characteristics (continued), CONT voltage (open circuit), VCC = 15V row, NA555, NE555, SA555 column
/pins/0/characteristics/open_circuit_vol.note: The 15 V column, transcribed from the 2026-10-24 retrieval of the same SLFS022K revision (re-served with new bytes). The VCC = 5 V element of this array is the original transcription under /pins.

/pins/3/capability.locator: Section 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, IO row; Features list, page 1
/pins/3/capability.note: The datasheet publishes no field named 'drive capability'. It states a recommended operating output current of +/-200 mA and an absolute-maximum of +/-225 mA, and the features list says the output 'can sink or source up to 200mA'. Capability is therefore recorded as max 200 mA - the recommended-operation limit - with the 225 mA stress limit kept separately in abs_max. Reading the 225 mA absolute maximum as drive capability would be a design error.

/pins/7/abs_max.note: The absolute maximum table gives 18 V as a MAX with no MIN, so no lower bound is recorded. The 4.5 V lower figure belongs to Recommended Operating Conditions and is recorded there instead - conflating the two would let a checker accept 4.5 V as a damage threshold.

/ratings/abs_max/esd_hbm.note: Published as +/-500 V, recorded as a symmetric interval.

/ratings/thermal/theta_ja.locator: Section 5.4 Thermal Information, RthetaJA row, P (PDIP) column
/ratings/thermal/theta_ja.note: Read from the rendered page of the 2026-10-24 retrieval. The P (PDIP) column is the only PDIP column and sits alone under the 'NA555, NE555' header cell; the PDF text layer flattens the merged header cells, which is why it once looked ambiguous. The table states no board construction (its note points to TI's thermal-metrics application report), so only the package is recorded as a condition.
